item.title: dotnet: Blazor Welcomes Open-Source Contributions from Syncfusion
item.description:
Microsoft and Syncfusion are collaborating on Blazor via a free open-source component toolkit, framework contributions, and developer tooling. The post says these contributions are now part of the Blazor ecosystem.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: dotnet: Blazor Welcomes Open-Source Contributions from Infragistics
item.description:
Microsoft and Infragistics are collaborating on Blazor with free open-source components, new .NET 11 analyzers, and developer tooling. The post announces these contributions on the .NET Blog.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Open source license compliance generally available
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Cloud now generally available for open source license compliance, with ruleset-based checks to enforce centralized licensing policy across dependencies.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: commandline: PyRIT: Democratizing AI red teaming through open-source tooling
item.description:
PyRIT is presented as an open-source Python tool for AI red teaming that lowers the barrier for subject matter experts to test generative AI systems. The article describes its evolution toward making red teaming more accessible across many domains.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: 🌿 Agent Terrarium: Bringing AI agents to life
item.description:
A weekend open-source desktop companion app, Agent Terrarium, explores a more interactive, less purely transactional way to work with AI agents.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: dotnet: From generated code to trusted code with a unit-test agent
item.description:
Microsoft introduced an open-source polyglot unit-testing agent that analyzes a repository, generates unit tests, and verifies that the tests build and pass. The post focuses on moving from generated code to code that is checked and trusted through automated testing.

  • Source: .NET
